title: Conditional Umegaki and complete equal-reference SLD order share a constant
statement: For finite-dimensional quantum channels P,Q with common input, uniform conditional Umegaki order is equivalent to complete equal-reference SLD metric order with the same constant, for arbitrary finite references. The necessity construction is a conditional-order argument with H_R=0 and deliberately different reference marginals. The coherent-qubit SLD-to-BKM integral is prior to Hirche, Proposition 3.5 / Eq. (3.18); the conditional reference-score gauge and reverse finite-filter construction are separate receiving steps.

requires: Two finite-dimensional channels with the same input.
Arbitrary finite reference, faithful baseline and zero-reference Hermitian tangent.
provides: Transfers a uniform conditional Umegaki comparison to complete equal-reference SLD order and back with unchanged c.
Keeps the Hirche integral attribution separate from the N966 conditional gauge and saturated-reference reverse-filter mechanism.
assumptions: Finite-dimensional states and channels; output states restricted to effective support; common faithful regularization for finite boundary pairs.
In the necessity construction, the tangent satisfies H_R=0 and the saturated auxiliary pair has different reference marginals.
Conditional deficits vanish at epsilon=0, allowing baseline subtraction for arbitrary c. The raw common baseline also cancels when c=1; this does not make the reference marginals equal.
The coherent-qubit integral is prior machinery. It does not supply the conditional gauge, reverse filter, or a positive equal-reference Umegaki witness by itself.
costs: A proof-level order interface; no acquisition, device, or computational efficiency is implied.
The finite-filter necessity construction has no uniform conditioning or precision bound.
contract.units: Dimensionless entropy contraction / SLD metric coefficient.
contract.obstruction: Does not equate the result to complete equal-reference Umegaki order for arbitrary quantum channels. Equal-marginal constraints obstruct the specified coherent saturated-reference filter, not all possible positive realizations or alternative constructions. The coherent-qubit integral is not an Astra novelty claim and does not by itself realize the reverse conditional witness as a positive equal-reference Umegaki pair.

body: N966 uses the saturated-reference filter only in the necessity direction, for H_R=0 and unequal reference marginals. Conditional deficits vanish at epsilon=0, so their common baseline cancels for arbitrary c; the raw common baseline also cancels in the special case c=1. The return implication uses the SLD reference-score gauge, SLD-to-BKM integral and state-pair interpolation. The coherent-qubit SLD-to-BKM integral is credited to Hirche, Proposition 3.5 / Eq. (3.18). N966's conditional reference-score gauge, saturated-reference reverse filter, and state-pair interpolation remain separate receiving steps with their own premises; the integral alone provides no equal-reference Umegaki witness.
